title: Install an Entry Light: Attic Run, Junction Box, and Sconce Wiring (This Old House)

locations.name: Attic
locations.basis: The team moves to the attic to access wiring and run new cable.

locations.name: Basement electrical panel
locations.basis: Power is cut at the circuit panel in the basement before starting work.

locations.name: Stud bay behind brick veneer wall
locations.basis: Plan is to route the new wire down into a stud wall behind a brick veneer and penetrate brick to install the sconce.

summary: This Old House demonstrates wiring a new entry light (sconce) by tracing the existing feed from the electrical panel to the switch, routing a new conductor through the attic, and down a stud wall behind a brick veneer to a new wall box. An attic junction box is installed for splices; conductors (ground, neutral, hot) are color-matched and joined with wire nuts, then the NM cable is fished down the wall, poked through holes in the stud bay, and secured with staples and firestopping. The sconce is mounted, grounded, and powered for a functional final install, with attention to code requirements and aesthetic placement aligned with Craftsman styling.
topics: Fixture placement relative to architectural features (mailbox alignment)
Tools: hammer, chisel, drill, hole saw

sections.description: The host and electrician trace the existing feed from the panel up to the wall switch and attic, discuss moving power to a new sconce, and outline a route: run a new box in the attic, pull a wire across, then down into the stud wall behind a brick veneer and through the brick to reach the new light.

sections.title: Wall routing, box installation, and final sconce mounting

sections.description: After finishing the attic work, the team fishes the new wire down the wall, marks the box location (centering it with the mailbox), drills holes around the electrical box, opens the wall as needed, pulls the Romex, and installs the box and lighting fixture, ends with a ground connection and power test.

sections.description: The crew confirms power is live to the new sconce and completes the final aesthetic and functional check.
